<noinclude><pagequality level="1" user="" />{{rh|114|THE GOSPEL|CHA. X.}}</noinclude>{{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=''Mt. 19, 16. Lu. 18, 18.''}}* Good Maister, vvhat shal I doe that I may receiue life euerlasting? {{verse|chapter=10|verse=18}}† And {{sc|Iesvs}} said to him, Why callest thou me good? {{sup|‖}} None is good but one, God. {{verse|chapter=10|verse=19}}† Thou knovvest the {{MarginNote|margin=left|margin-width=65|text=∷ Note that the keeping of Gods cōmaundements procureth life euerlasting.}}∷ commaundements, {{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=''Exo. 20, 13.''}}* ''Commit not aduoutrie, Kil not, Steale not, Beare not false vvitnesse, doe no fraude, Honour thy father and mother''. {{verse|chapter=10|verse=20}}† But he ansvvering, said to him, Maister al these things I haue obserued from my youth. {{verse|chapter=10|verse=21}}† And {{sc|Iesvs}} beholding him, loued him, and said to him, One thing is vvanting vnto thee: {{MarginNote|margin=left|margin-width=65|text=∷ This is counsel of perfectiō (not a precept) which the Religious professing and keeping voluntary pouertie, doe folow.}}∷ goe, sel vvhatsoeuer thou hast, and giue to the poore, and thou shalt haue treasure in heauen: and come, folovv me. {{verse|chapter=10|verse=22}}† Who being stroken sad at the vvord, vvent avvay sorovvful. for he had many possessions. {{verse|chapter=10|verse=23}}† And {{sc|Iesvs}} looking about, saith to his Disciples, Hovv hardly shal they that haue money, enter into the kingdom of God! {{verse|chapter=10|verse=24}}† And the Disciples vvere astonied at his vvordes. But {{sc|Iesvs}} againe ansvvering, saith to them, Children, hovv hard is it for them that trust in money, to enter into the kingdom of God! {{verse|chapter=10|verse=25}}† It is easier for a camel to passe through a nedels eie, then for {{sup|‖}} a rich man to enter into the kingdom of God. {{verse|chapter=10|verse=26}}† VVho marueled more, saying to them selues, And vvho can be saued? {{verse|chapter=10|verse=27}}† And {{sc|Iesvs}} beholding them, saith, VVith men it is impossibile: but not vvith God. for al things are possible vvith God. {{verse|chapter=10|verse=28}}† And Peter began to say vnto him, Behold, vve haue left al things, and haue folovved thee. {{verse|chapter=10|verse=29}}† {{sc|Iesvs}} ansvvering, said, {{MarginNote|margin=left|margin-width=65|text=∷ Exceding happie be they that can forsake their temporal things for religion.}}∷ Amen I say to you, there is no man vvhich hath left house, or brethren, or sisters, or father, or mother, or children, or landes for me and for the Gospel: {{verse|chapter=10|verse=30}}† that shal not receiue {{sup|‖}} an hundred times so much novv in this time: houses, and brethren, and sisters, and mothers, and children, and landes, vvith persecutions: and in the vvorld to come life euerlasting. {{verse|chapter=10|verse=31}}† But {{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=''Mt. 19, 30. Lu. 13, 30.''}}* many that are first, shal be last: and the last, first.

{{verse|chapter=10|verse=32}}† And they vvere in the vvay going vp to Hierusalem: and {{sc|Iesvs}} vvent before them, and they vvere astonied: and folovving vvere afraid. And {{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=''Mt. 20, 17. Lu. 18, 31.''}}* taking againe the Tvvelue, he began to tel them the things that should befal him. {{verse|chapter=10|verse=33}}† That, behold vve goe vp to Hierusalem, and the Sonne of man shal be betrayed to the cheefe Priestes, and to the Scribes and Auncients, and they shal condemne him to death, and shal deliuer him to the Gentiles, {{verse|chapter=10|verse=34}}† and they shal mocke him, and spit on him, and scourge him, and kil him, and the third day he shal rise againe.<noinclude>{{rh|||And}}</noinclude>
